title: Most-cited OSHA standards for warehousing and storage (NAICS 4931)
seoTitle: Warehouse OSHA citations: NAICS 4931 top standards
description: OSHA standards cited most in warehousing and storage (NAICS 4931), FY2022–FY2026: powered industrial trucks lead, with penalty median and citation types.
opening: In warehousing and storage (NAICS 4931), 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks, is the OSHA standard cited most, with 1,345 citations in FY2022–FY2026, ahead of 1910.1200 Hazard communication at 455 and 1910.303 electrical general requirements at 446.
patternsSummary: Materials handling is the clearest pattern in warehousing and storage: 1910.178 Powered industrial trucks (1,345 citations) and 1910.176 Handling materials—general (243) both come from Subpart N, Materials Handling and Storage. Electrical rules are the next group, with 1910.303 General (446) and 1910.305 Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use (352) from Subpart S. Emergency readiness forms a third group: 1910.37 exit route maintenance and safeguards (436), 1910.157 Portable fire extinguishers (333) and 1910.36 exit route design and construction (115).
penaltiesSummary: The median penalty for warehousing and storage citations in FY2022–FY2026 is $5,358, and the middle half of penalties falls between $2,500 and $9,045. Serious citations make up 57% of the total, other-than-serious 42%, repeat 1% and willful 0% after rounding.

standardNotes.note: Powered industrial trucks, in Subpart N (Materials Handling and Storage); the most-cited standard here, with 1,345 citations.
Hazard communication, part of Subpart Z (Toxic and Hazardous Substances); cited 455 times.
General requirements of Subpart S (Electrical); 446 citations.
Maintenance, safeguards and operational features for exit routes, from Subpart E (Exit Routes and Emergency Planning); 436 citations.
Wiring methods, components and equipment for general use, also in Subpart S (Electrical); cited 352 times.
Portable fire extinguishers, under Subpart L (Fire Protection); 333 citations.
Handling materials—general, the second Subpart N standard in the top list; cited 243 times.
General requirements for personal protective equipment, Subpart I; 192 citations.
